regime_context: The detector shows a broad but mixed leadership structure headed by Big Banks (rank 1, eligible, durable trend) with Oil & Gas Producers as the closest challenger (rank 2 but ineligible). The only validated edge is drawdown control via the absolute-trend gate, which is active and historically helpful on this market; cross-sectional momentum rank is a focus lens, not alpha. Track record shows a 0.313 directional accuracy over 147 calls — low directional skill despite a 0.558 hit rate — so I default to modest conviction with conditionals.
emerging_watch: Watching Oil & Gas Producers (rank 2, score 0.915, challenger with 0.103 margin). It is currently ineligible (durability 0.23, breadth 0.214, mixed Hurst). I will treat the challenger as a confirmed handoff only if it becomes eligible (trend-gate passes) AND its durability_bar rises above roughly 0.6 while Big Banks' durability concurrently drops — otherwise the leadership remains with banks.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the only high-durability, eligible, trend-tagged theme at the top of the rank (rank 1, durability 0.8, breadth 1.0, Hurst 'trend', not crowded). It sits on the correct side of the absolute-trend gate, which is the one validated risk-control leg in this market's history. The lean is a pure trend-continuation judgement: leadership is concentrated and cohesive, but I am not reading the score as a forecast of returns.
theses.dissent: Banks are exactly the kind of rate-sensitive, high-beta-to-macro theme that gets sold first if the dominant coincident macro narrative is AI/tech plus unscheduled geopolitical shocks (unscheduled_share 0.91); a broad risk-off would hit the leader hardest precisely because it is the leader.

theses.subject: Consumer Staples & Retail
theses.thesis: Third-ranked and eligible with the highest durability in the table (0.82), full breadth (1.0), and a trend Hurst tag — a rare combination. This is a defensive quality-trend theme that validates on the absolute-trend gate (the one edge this market has). Crowding is moderate (0.91) but below the threshold, so it is a size-down caution at most, not a fade.
theses.dissent: Staples leadership can be a sign of late-cycle defensiveness rather than genuine trend; if the broader TSX is in a risk-on AI-led tape, defensives may lag precisely because they protect rather than participate.

falsifier.text: XST.TO loses 4% relative to the S&P/TSX over any 20-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Utilities & Renewables
theses.thesis: Eligible, durable trend (0.8), high breadth (0.917), and the least crowded theme in the upper half of the table (crowding_z -0.25). It passes the absolute-trend gate, which is the one leg with validated drawdown control on this market. The lean is purely a stay-in-the-trend call: it is not a forecast of strong returns.
theses.dissent: Renewables and utilities can trade as bond-proxy rate-sensitives; if the coincident macro backdrop tilts back to rising-rate or inflation-shock headline domination, this theme may underperform the broad benchmark despite its internal trend health.
